nodes.name: Check config
nodes.notes: Why Code: validates the loaded config so a bad value fails loudly instead of silently disabling a check

parameters.query:
-- Records a newly seen Gmail attachment once. A replayed poll for the same event (a node retry,
-- or an owner retry from the n8n UI) is suppressed by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING instead of raising a
-- duplicate-key error. On the SQL side that's zero rows, but this is an INSERT, not a SELECT, so
-- n8n's Postgres node reports it as one {success: true} item with no event_id, not as zero items.
-- Parameters, in order: event_id (text), file_name (text)
INSERT INTO processed_events (source, event_id, file_name)
VALUES ('gmail', $1, $2)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
RETURNING event_id, to_jsonb(received_at) #>> '{}' AS received_at;

parameters.content:
## Intake new mail
Called once per poll with every new email from that poll, still as separate items. Loads the config once for the whole batch, checks it, and attaches it to every item before anything else runs.

## One item per PDF
Splits each email into one item per attachment, then keeps only what the rest of the workflow needs: a stable event id, the message id, which binary holds the file, and its name and MIME type.

## Idempotency gate
Keeps only PDF attachments, records each one's event id once, and lets through only the attachments that were newly recorded - so a re-polled or re-delivered attachment never reaches Process invoice twice.

## Process
Calls Process invoice once per surviving attachment, so one bad PDF fails only its own call. That sub-workflow already fires its own error email; this one just continues with the rest of the batch.

NOTE: if this INSERT commits but its response is lost before n8n sees it, a retry - this node's own, or a UI retry of the whole execution - re-runs the same INSERT, which ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING now suppresses; since that's a non-SELECT query returning no rows, the node reports a bare {success: true} item with no event_id, so Keep new attachments finds no match for it - the event looks already known even though it was never processed. It shows up only as unfinished, with no error email. Recovery: delete that event's row from processed_events, then forward the source email again so Gmail delivers it as new mail.
